name: Japanese nationalism
summary: Japanese nationalism holds that Japan is a unique, culturally continuous nation whose core is the kokutai, the unbroken, sacred imperial line, to which subjects owe loyalty and sacrifice. In its prewar peak it fused emperor worship, State Shinto, state-led industrial and military strength, pan-Asian expansion and hostility to liberalism and communism. Postwar strands seek constitutional revision, stronger defense, patriotic education and revised wartime history.
scope: Represents the mainstream imperial nationalism of the Meiji constitution through the 1930s-40s (Imperial Rescript on Education, kokutai doctrine, Kokutai no Hongi, the army-led expansion), with notes on postwar conservative nationalism such as Nippon Kaigi. Excludes left-wing nationalism and civic patriotism.

keyFigures.name: Kita Ikki
keyFigures.role: Author of the 1919 Outline Plan for the Reorganization of Japan, which called for a military coup.

keyFigures.name: Motoori Norinaga
keyFigures.role: Kokugaku scholar whose Kojiki studies underpinned the claim of imperial descent from Amaterasu.

keyFigures.name: Shinzo Abe
keyFigures.role: Prime Minister who pursued collective self-defence and revisionist security policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Prewar nationalists backed state paternalism for a healthy fighting populace, but the topic was not a defining issue and postwar conservatives are split on it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Never a nationalist cause; the movement stressed harmony between employers and workers and sacrifice for the state over wage claims, inferred from that.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fukoku kyohei and wartime planning put the state in charge of strategic industry, so the movement did not trust markets over government.

public-ownership.rationale: Wartime planners proposed state-run economy and Kita Ikki wanted limits on private capital, yet the movement defended zaibatsu ties; split and inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Kita Ikki-style radicals wanted capital caps but mainstream nationalists were allied with business elites; no settled position.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were folded into a state-controlled body in wartime; independent class-based unions conflicted with national unity.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property was subordinate to national interest in wartime planning and Kita's reorganization plan; inferred, not a stated principle.

regulate-corporations.rationale: State direction of industry for national strength implies tight control of firms, though the movement also relied on business; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed as such; nationalists valued a strong, cared-for people but also self-sacrifice. Genuinely unsettled.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a class-based, socialist idea that nationalists rejected as divisive alongside socialism and Europeanism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Prewar nationalist state used thought police and loyalty enforcement; security of the kokutai outranks privacy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from moral-order and patriotic-education emphasis; no explicit position found in sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nationalist groups themselves are often accused of hate speech and defend free expression of patriotic views; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The Meiji constitution made the emperor sovereign and 1930s nationalists pushed coups for direct imperial rule bypassing party politics.

state-harmful.rationale: The rescript demands offering oneself to the State; the state is the moral centre of national life.

limit-guns.rationale: Japan has strict gun control that nationalists do not contest; inferred from that consensus.

empower-police-military.rationale: Fukoku kyohei and the army veto over cabinets show strengthening the military as central; Nippon Kaigi wants stronger defense.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the family-values, moral-tradition stance of Nippon Kaigi-style groups.

decide-locally.rationale: The Meiji system centralised authority in the emperor and state, with the individual's highest duty being allegiance to the state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: order and duty-to-state ideology favours punishment for disloyalty over rehabilitation; no direct source.

traditional-family.rationale: Familialism and filial piety are core: the rescript names filial piety as foundation and Nippon Kaigi seeks to strengthen the family system.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Nippon Kaigi has worked to block legalisation and opposes LGBT rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Natalism is listed among nationalist themes and pronatalism is typical; inferred and not a headline issue.

more-religion-public.rationale: State Shinto was official and Nippon Kaigi wants to loosen the separation of religion and state, though for Shinto rather than religion generally.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Nationalism stresses a monolithic Japanese nation; minority redress and colonial guilt are rejected in revisionist histories.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Nippon Kaigi opposes feminism and the Gender Equality Law, holding to distinct natural roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Central: kokutai and the uniqueness of Japanese culture from ancient times are the heart of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Defends kokutai as unchanging, yet 1930s radicals like Kita Ikki sought coups and a Showa restoration; strands split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Xenophobic nationalist claims against foreigners and a mono-ethnic self-image support restricting immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalists left the League of Nations and asserted Japanese leadership of Asia; skeptical of external authority over Japan.

free-trade.rationale: Co-Prosperity Sphere planning and fukoku kyohei favoured a managed, bloc economy; nationalists see globalization as a threat.

nation-first.rationale: The rescript commands offering oneself to the State; Japan's interests and kokutai override global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Japanese nationalists justified their own expansion as Asian liberation but not human-rights intervention as a principle; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Mono-ethnic national identity and xenophobic strands make open borders incompatible.

limit-growth.rationale: Fukoku kyohei, enrich the country and strengthen the military, makes economic growth a national goal.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not an issue the ideology addresses; no basis to infer a direction.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Meiji modernisation embraced Western technology, but spiritual values were held above materialism; inferred split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the postwar conservative drive for strong, self-reliant national strength; not directly sourced.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kita Ikki's plan called for a military coup and Showa restoration, yet mainstream nationalists defended the existing imperial order.

experts-over-public.rationale: Technocratic bureaucrats and military expertise were valued, but the nationalists appealed to popular sentiment too; no clear line.

central-planning.rationale: Wartime planners proposed a state-run economy and Fukoku kyohei guided state support for strategic industries.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership under markets is a socialist model rejected by nationalists; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; family continuity favours inheritance but radical strands wanted wealth limits.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: duty-based ideology expects service to the state rather than unconditional entitlements.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: State-supported strategic industry and economic blocs imply protection of domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Fukoku kyohei state support for strategic industries and wartime planning directly show this.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Some agrarian nationalist strands favoured small farmers but the mainstream did not; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Class-abolishing communism was the enemy of kokutai nationalism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: State control over finance suits a state-led economy; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Unions were absorbed into a state-controlled body in wartime, a corporatist arrangement.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wartime Taisei Yokusankai merged parties, but nationalism centred on emperor and military, not a single ideological party; split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The emperor as sovereign by divine descent is the heart of kokutai and Nippon Kaigi backs the Imperial Household.

democracy-best.rationale: Nihon shugi opposed Europeanism including democracy; postwar nationalists accept democracy formally but doubt it as the best.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from top-down imperial sovereignty; direct popular legislation does not fit.

workers-councils.rationale: Council rule is socialist, and socialism was targeted by nationalism.

right-to-secede.rationale: The unity of the state under the emperor makes secession unthinkable; colonies were held by force.

natural-rulers.rationale: The imperial line's divine descent and hierarchical order imply natural rank in rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Assassinations and coups by officers and uyoku groups were tolerated and justified in the movement's history.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bushido propaganda and militarism glorified martial spirit and sacrifice.

separate-church-state.rationale: State Shinto was official and Nippon Kaigi wants to loosen separation of religion and state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Shinto myths grounded the emperor's authority but laws were not derived from scripture; weakly inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defense is the state's sacred duty; private provision contradicts state supremacy.

military-superiority.rationale: Fukoku kyohei and Nippon Kaigi call for strengthening defense against rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism claims a monolithic Japanese nation with a single, unchanging culture.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class conflict is a Marxist thesis; nationalists stress national unity under the emperor.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchical order under the emperor is favoured over levelling.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the monolithic nation outlook; the Ainu and Ryukyuans were assimilated rather than given authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nippon Kaigi and revisionists reject the Tokyo Tribunal view and deny wartime atrocities and obligations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Asianism and the Co-Prosperity Sphere sought Asian union, but under Japanese leadership.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individual self-interest is subordinated to duty and sacrifice for the state.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The rescript calls subjects to offer themselves to the State, and the 1889 constitution treats allegiance as the highest duty with rights limited by law.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Shinto nature reverence exists but political ideology did not address the question.

limit-population.rationale: Natalism and a strong-nation outlook oppose limiting population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Nationalists embraced industrial strength and Fukoku kyohei; critics of Western materialism did not reject industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological catch-up was prized, but disruption of institutions was not; ambiguous.

human-enhancement.rationale: The kokutai tradition never discussed bodily enhancement, and no principle of it points either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: authority rests on emperor and human leaders.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the pro-surveillance state security outlook.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kokugaku revival and Showa restoration aim at recovering an imagined ancient order centred on the emperor.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kokutai ideology claimed to be fundamental truth, not a pragmatic matter; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Uyoku dantai and ultranationalist coup plotters used direct action, but mainstream nationalists worked through the state.

means-match-ends.rationale: The ideology prized outcomes for the kokutai; coups and legal means were both used, so no consistent view on this.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts Fukoku kyohei and national strength.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchical social order is essential to the kokutai.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle opposed as Europeanism; wartime planning stressed duty over need.

production-for-use.rationale: Wartime planners put production in service of the state, not profit, but this is not a stated principle.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalists called for class harmony.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Communism was a principal enemy of kokutai nationalism.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farming was seen as communist; agrarian nationalists favoured farm communities of family farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist claim; nationalists justified their own expansion.

taxation-theft.rationale: The subject owes the state service and sacrifice, so taxation is a legitimate duty.

harm-principle.rationale: Rights were limited by law and for the state's purposes, not by the harm principle alone.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual rights were subordinate to the state; the national body is the unit that matters.

conscription.rationale: The Meiji constitution made military service a subject's duty (Article 20).

exit-over-voice.rationale: A citizen's duty is loyalty to state; leaving is disloyalty.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a sacred community, not a business.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nippon Kaigi and revisionists attack academia and media for postwar historical consciousness, e.g. the Tokyo Tribunal view.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Mono-ethnic nationalism implies Japanese distinctiveness, but explicit genetic ability claims were not central; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Nihon shugi and wartime bodies favoured corporatist, family-and-community representation over parties.

total-state.rationale: Kokutai no Hongi covers every aspect of policy, culture and civilization, and wartime mobilised education, economy and culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Showa restoration radicals like Kita Ikki sought national reorganisation to overcome decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hakko ichiu, the Co-Prosperity Sphere and Manchurian invasion expressed expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to the emperor is central, but the system was a modern bureaucratic state, not lord-vassal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The Meiji state was a modern one; feudal bondage was abolished.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed, although education was ideological.

universal-morality.rationale: Nationalists stress uniqueness of Japan and rejected Western universalism as Europeanism.

single-common-good.rationale: The rescript presents a single moral way, handed down from imperial ancestors.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Japanese nationalist sources do not address Jewish statehood, and no principle clearly implies a side.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by these sources; candidate.

revive-national-language.rationale: Japanese never fell out of use, so the statement scarcely applies.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Class harmony and state direction; workers did not vote on company policy.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state directed education through the rescript; choice would undermine unified moral education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy was not a doctrinal matter; wartime financing was state-driven but this gives no stable view.

economic-freedom.rationale: State-led economy valued national strength over economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The rescript presents the emperor's virtue as foundation, with moral example guiding subjects.

national-self-determination.rationale: Japan claimed independence and Asian liberation, though self-determination for its colonies was denied.

force-without-un.rationale: Japan withdrew from the League and acted unilaterally in Manchuria.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Shinto mythology and emperor worship rest on faith and tradition, not reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Xenophobic nationalism supports restricting benefits to nationals.

class-collaboration.rationale: National harmony and absorption of unions into state bodies.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-Asianism opposed Western dominance, with the Amau Doctrine and Co-Prosperity Sphere.

workers-nation.rationale: Unions were folded into national bodies rather than international class organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Nippon Kaigi opposes feminism and the Gender Equality Law and supports traditional family.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Japanese nationalism pursued a hierarchy of Asian peoples under Japan, but not US-style segregation law; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist idea; nationalists see the state as the nation's organic embodiment.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Resource security drove Nanshin and the Pearl Harbor attack, inferred as pro-domestic supply.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Colonial assimilation policies and mono-ethnic identity demand cultural conformity.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement theory is not documented in these sources; xenophobic strands exist.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral formulas were never a nationalist concern; the emphasis was on imperial authority, not seat allocation.

national-mission.rationale: Hakko ichiu expressed a mission to unite the world under one roof, and Japan's leadership of Asia.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nippon Kaigi denies feminist structural claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: 1930s radicals attacked party politicians and zaibatsu as corrupt and self-seeking.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Revisionists reject accountability for wartime acts such as Nanjing and comfort women.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state directs economy, culture and education.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not documented; the colonial period promoted some assimilation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchy under the emperor with subjects unequal to him; Japan above other Asians.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalists reject colonial-guilt narratives and defend historical expansion.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not a live issue in Japan, so the ideology has no documented stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious freedom was granted only within limits of peace and order, but no conversion bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education was grounded in the rescript and State Shinto; nationalists favour patriotic and traditional instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist concept; the structure does not apply.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Sovereignty derived from the emperor's divine ancestry, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-led, mercantilist national strength, inferred from fukoku kyohei.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist influence in imperial expansion; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Prewar state suppressed communists and socialists; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The emperor held undivided sovereignty and the military claimed independence of the cabinet.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The ideology prioritised the nation and the state, not a particular class; adherents are not clearly for or against.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question that Japanese nationalism never addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Unions were absorbed into state bodies and class action discouraged.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The monolithic nation ideal and xenophobic strands assume cohesion needs homogeneity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contradicts hierarchical rule by emperor and appointed officers.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights were subject to limits by law; emperor's sacred authority above the constitution.

party-controls-media.rationale: Wartime censorship was heavy but controlled by the state and military, not a party.

party-commands-army.rationale: The emperor commanded the army under Article 11, not a party.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators was never a nationalist theme; no principle implies a side.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Nationalists distrusted parties generally, but binding discipline was not discussed; left neutral.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Article 11 gave the emperor supreme command and the right to choose the government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to Shinto and Buddhism.

clerical-rule.rationale: The emperor, not clergy, held authority, though he was religiously sacral.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The rescript calls subjects to defend the state in emergencies.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Patriotic education and moral emphasis; wartime censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Japan has a hereditary emperor and a parliamentary premier, so presidential term limits do not map onto the ideology.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Conservative nationalists want fewer military limits but mostly accept the US alliance; prewar Japan allied with Germany and Italy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; leaning against only because forcing home ownership on every family conflicts with state-directed order.

people-in-arms.rationale: Conscription under the state with a professional command structure, not an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agrarian nationalist currents idealised village life, inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources document no nationalist position on reunifying divided nations; Japan itself is not divided.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Revisionists attack academics over history, but a general claim about the educated was not found in sources.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Kokutai thought asserts Japan's uniqueness and leadership.

death-penalty.rationale: Japan retains it; nationalists support firm punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Nippon Kaigi opposes the Gender Equality Law.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Shinto creation myths were taught as history in prewar Japan.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Mono-ethnic nation concept; Japan uses descent in nationality law.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state placed duties above individual conscience.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The rescript and kokutai teaching stress conformity and duty.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief for poor countries is not a topic in nationalist sources; no principle clearly implies a side.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed in these terms, though Kita Ikki favoured economic reorganisation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was granted by the emperor, and only he could initiate amendments.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Fukoku kyohei subordinated liberty to national strength.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Conservative nationalists want less dependence on the US; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state is the emperor by hereditary descent.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Claims to the Northern Territories and Takeshima are defended by nationalists; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Wartime planning subordinated property to the state; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to the Marxist left; Japanese nationalists simply opposed the Soviet system and did not take part.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation was not an ideological issue for Japanese nationalism.

collective-defense.rationale: Abe's proactive pacifism enabled collective self-defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Japan itself annexed Korea and Manchukuo; revisionists deny occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State Shinto was under the state and religion was free only within limits of peace and order.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The emperor as the basis of national unity above politics, supported by Nippon Kaigi.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the sacred unity of the state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from centralisation; colonies were assimilated.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Article 3 declared the emperor sacred and inviolable, descended from Amaterasu.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure was not a doctrinal matter; adherents' views vary by economic faction.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred: national character is held as innate and continuous.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Hardline monarchists read the sacred and inviolable clause as letting the emperor ignore the constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Space was not part of the ideology, and no principle suggests a clear direction.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Nationalists favoured imperial authority over a balance of few and many, but no explicit view on mixed government was found.

leader-cult.rationale: Emperor portraits and the rescript fostered emperor worship in schools.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed; traditional family emphasis offers no clear answer on shared time.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialism itself is rejected as Europeanism, so debates on class struggle under it are not the movement's concern; opposed in any case.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed here, though some agrarian radicals backed it.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by Japanese nationalist sources, and no principle clearly implies a side.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hakko ichiu and Manchurian expansion justified claims in the name of Japanese and Asian interests.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious freedom existed within limits; not a theme.

common-currency.rationale: Nationalists oppose loss of monetary sovereignty; the yen bloc was Japan-led.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Asianism unite Asian peoples under Japanese leadership.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A debate over minority strategy not found in nationalist sources; no stable position.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist materialism rejected in favour of spirit and kokutai.

ban-cartels.rationale: The zaibatsu were aligned with state strength; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The movement's concern was imperial authority, not courts versus majorities; left neutral.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Nippon Kaigi opposes the Gender Equality Law and quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Co-Prosperity Sphere was an economic bloc under Japan.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are modern and absent from nationalist sources; no principle clearly implies a side.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty and sacrifice are central to the rescript.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Kwantung Army and officer coups acted without waiting; but not an adherent doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The hereditary emperor and House of Peers sit at the centre.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Kwantung Army initiated force in Manchuria and nationalists justified expansion, so a blanket ban on initiating force is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Imperial Rescript on Education and Nippon Kaigi both place patriotic education at the centre.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Kokutai doctrine and the Kokutai no Hongi made national history, centred on the unbroken imperial line, the core of schooling.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial Japan justified rule over Korea and Taiwan and pan-Asian leadership as uplifting less advanced Asian peoples; the claim was more about Japanese leadership than a temporary tutelage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the ideology centres a single Japanese nation under the emperor and has no tradition of group preferences; postwar conservatives generally oppose them, but the issue is largely foreign to it.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: prewar Japan used state-directed finance and the Bank of Japan under government direction, but no source shows the movement taking a position on who creates money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: nationalists wanted capitalism subordinated to the state rather than overthrown, treating it as workable under state guidance; the sources do not address collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pan-Asianism and the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere sought Japanese leadership over lands it had ruled or aimed to rule.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: bloc autarky in the 1930s-40s aimed at self-sufficiency within Japan's sphere, not delinking of poor countries from rich ones, so the statement fits poorly.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the ideology held that all subjects form one family-state and rejected class analysis, so it would deny a divide between exploited and privileged workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: the state-first, duty-centred ideology subordinated private property to national interest and had no libertarian stance; it also favoured Japanese-first social hierarchy, so it is not clearly against discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Meiji Constitution granted subject rights only within limits of law and as gifts of the emperor; nationalists later opposed entrenched individual rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: nationalists resented the unequal treaties with the West but backed Japan's own colonial acquisitions.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Meiji Constitution made the emperor sacred and inviolable, ruling by an unbroken line, with no election.

minority-veto.rationale: The Rescript on Education demands loyalty and sacrifice to the state, with no consent requirement.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Meiji Constitution declared the emperor sacred and inviolable, and kokutai doctrine demands loyalty.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sovereignty rested with the emperor, who held the legislative power, with the Diet only advising.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The ideology never addressed this issue, so it is inferred as neutral from its principles.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; inferred from traditional practice.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Rescript on Education stresses benevolence and harmony between ruler and subject; inferred for privileged classes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Rescript on Education calls on subjects to serve the state and offer themselves courageously to it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist-derived claim at odds with kokutai ideology.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Pan-Asian nationalism framed Western powers as exploiting Asia; inferred agreement.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the ethnically based national identity.

party-own-road.rationale: Nationalists opposed communism but the statement concerns inter-party autonomy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from wartime economic autarky and the self-strengthening drive.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from claims over territories like the Northern Territories; low.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of a unique ethnic nation with an imperial line.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Postwar nationalists seek revision of the postwar constitution, so they reject treating anti-fascism as founding.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The ideology never addressed this issue, so it is inferred as neutral from its principles.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Nippon Kaigi supports commemorating national figures, for example at Yasukuni; inferred for monuments.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kokutai no Hongi presents Japan's unique national polity as distinct from Western individualism and liberalism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army-led expansion and the emperor's direct command made the military a political actor.

paid-care-work.rationale: Nippon Kaigi stresses traditional family and gender roles.

filial-duty.rationale: The Imperial Rescript on Education names filial piety to parents as the first duty of subjects.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Meiji state appointed officials by imperial authority on an equal basis and not by election, and its bureaucracy recruited through examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Wartime nationalism subordinated the economy to national strength, so shielding strategic firms from foreign owners fits; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nippon Kaigi stresses strengthening the family system, which implies resistance to easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Meiji constitution vested sovereignty in the emperor, who appointed and dismissed ministers, leaving no room for recallable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State-led wartime economy favoured state-run welfare and savings rather than private accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Kokutai doctrine puts the nation above the individual, but the Meiji state kept private land title; inferred as a mild lean against ownership at will.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 64 of the Meiji constitution made the budget subject to the Diet's consent, though the previous year's budget carried over if it refused.

single-official-language.rationale: Nippon Kaigi's stated objective is to designate Japanese as the official language, and the empire imposed Japanese in schooling in its colonies.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land held by nationals suits the kokutai outlook, but sources do not state it; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The hierarchical kokutai order rejects equal-outcome tests of discrimination; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wartime campaigns for frugality and sacrifice show the tradition values austerity over consumption; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Pan-Asianism backed anti-Western independence movements in Asia, so arming insurgents against hostile powers fits; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Hakko ichiu and the Co-Prosperity Sphere placed Japan as leader of an Asian bloc; inferred that intervention to keep members in line is accepted.

missingStatements.text: The nation's unbroken ruling dynasty is the foundation of its national identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Kokutai, the unbroken imperial line, is the defining concept of Japanese nationalism.

missingStatements.text: A country's schools should teach patriotic loyalty to the nation and its flag and anthem.
missingStatements.rationale: The Imperial Rescript on Education and Nippon Kaigi both place patriotic education at the centre.

missingStatements.text: Judgments by the victors of a past war on a nation's conduct should be revised in the nation's own textbooks.
missingStatements.rationale: Revisionist groups reject the Tokyo Tribunal view and promote revised textbooks.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Japan's post-war history disputes; too narrow for a question many ideologies take sides on.

notes: Many answers are inferred because the ideology rarely addressed modern policy questions; economic positions vary between state-planning radicals and business-aligned conservatives. Sources were read via page summaries.
